Hi Sofia — thanks for the sample, that’s perfect to get started. A few technical follow-ups and examples to help your engineers: 

1) Typical integration pattern (candidate generation + rerank):
- Stage A: generate candidate_ids (N candidates, commonly 10–50).
- Stage B: call Redwood Rerank API with the query + candidate payload. Redwood returns scores + optional structured output (reason tags).

2) Example rerank request (pseudo-HTTP):
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
Body (JSON):
{
  "query": "red shoes size 10",
  "candidates": ["id_123","id_456","id_789"],
  "top_k": 10,
  "return_structured": true
}

Notes: top_k indicates how many final items you want in the ranked response. For evaluation, we recommend returning scores for the full candidate set (so you can compute metrics at different k). If you set top_k smaller than the incoming candidate count, Redwood will still score all candidates but return the top_k subset if you request it.

3) Auth / SDK setup:
- For hosted Redwood: API keys scoped to rerank; keys can be rotated in Console.
- For Dedicated: use mTLS or VPC linking; we can provide short-lived tokens via your identity provider.
- SDK: our JS/py SDKs include a rerank helper that accepts a list of candidate objects and can stream partial results for low-latency UX.

4) Evaluation metrics we recommend (offline):
- Recall@k (k=1,5,10)
- MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
- NDCG@k for graded relevance (if you have relevance labels)
- Precision@k and CTR uplift simulation (if click labels are available)

Suggested default tuning: start with evaluating candidate sizes [10, 20, 50] and compute Recall@k and MRR. If you have click data, simulate top-1 CTR changes using existing logs. We typically see diminishing returns past top 50 for reranking quality vs cost.

5) Latency considerations:
- If you need p95 < 150ms for rerank alone, keep candidate sets <= 20 and enable batching and caching where appropriate.
- We can provide quantized model variants (8-bit) to reduce latency/cost for large volumes.

6) Next data asks from our side:
- Query distribution (freq buckets), typical candidate set sizes, and 1k–5k labeled examples if possible.

If it helps, here’s a short script we use for offline scoring:

// pseudo-Python for offline scoring
for q in queries:
  scores = api.rerank(query=q.text, candidates=q.candidate_ids, return_scores=True)
  compute_metrics(q.labels, scores)

Happy to jump on the tech session and walk through the SDK and a live run in your environment.

—Dev
